newsitem.title: UK: Windfall cash may boost UK housing upswing - survey.
newsitem.headline: Windfall cash may boost UK housing upswing - survey.

text.p: One in ten Britons intends to buy a new home in the next year, with a significant number using windfall cash from building society conversions, the Alliance & Leicester Plc said on Tuesday.
In a new six-monthly survey, "The Homebuyers' Report" it found that 28 percent of all adults said that a bonus or windfall was most likely to help them on their way to buying a new home.

"It seems that external factors such as the prospects of higher interest rates and house price fluctuations are less of an influence on people's ability to move than cash in their pockets," the survey said.
But the survey found one in four homeowners who would like to move house were deterred from doing so because of a variety of economic and market factors.

"Most people (47 percent) in this group said they could not afford to. A further 13 percent said that they could not find a property to buy and 8.0 percent cannot sell their existing property," it said.
Only 2.0 percent mentioned negative equity as a reason for delaying their move.
